doc.title: John Lamb interviewed by Monk Rowe, Clearwater Beach, Florida, March 16, 2001

title: Hearing Boston's jazz clubs: Hi-Hat and Storyville
summary: He hears Miles, Ella, Basie, Duke, Parker, Prez and Jimmy Woode at the Hi-Hat and Storyville.

story.theme_name: Coming to New York: clubs, jams, and making it
story.community_name: Making it in New York: arrival, clubs and the scene

blocks.x: Storyville. George Wein owned that. And the big man in town was Jimmy Woode, the bass player, and Junior Raglin, whenever Duke would come to town would come by and sit and play. And I’d listen to these guys and I’m beginning to pick up on what they — I says now what’s so appealing about that? I says I can do that. And so on. And got a chance to hear Basie over at Storyville and I heard Duke and I heard Charlie Parker and Prez along with Duke’s band, and the singers, Joe Williams, and that thing “Every Day” that they put out.
Yes. I used to go up to the jukebox late at night and listen to that all the time, listen to that bass player, Ed Jones. Remember Ed Jones?
